title: To Acquire Wisdom: The Way of Wang Yang-ming
author: Julia Ching
citation_detail: Ching, Julia. To Acquire Wisdom: The Way of Wang Yang-ming. Studies in Oriental Culture, No. 11. New York: Columbia University Press, 1976. ISBN 0-231-03968-7. xxvi + 373 pp. Based on Ching's 1971 ANU doctoral dissertation (6 chapters, no Japan coverage in dissertation). Published version revised and expanded; Part Three and concluding chapter reportedly discuss Wang Yangming's legacy including transmission to Japan. VERIFICATION NOTE (2026-05-13): Exact page references for Nakae Tōju, Japanese Yangmingism, and late Tokugawa figures could not be verified through online sources. The 1971 ANU dissertation (open access) does NOT discuss Japan at all. Japan material, if present, exists only in the published 1976 book. Ching's 1984 journal article (see SRC016) provides verified coverage of Nakae Tōju specifically.
note: Standard English-language monograph on Wang Yangming. Covers life, philosophical development, core doctrines. Japanese Yangmingism coverage: reported in Part Three and concluding chapter (published book only, not in dissertation). Page refs unverified — physical book access required. For verified Nakae Tōju coverage, see SRC016 (Ching 1984). For late Tokugawa figures (C026), SRC014 remains primary source but requires page verification.

title: The Idea of God in Nakae Toju
author: Julia Ching
citation_detail: Ching, Julia. "The Idea of God in Nakae Tōju." Japanese Journal of Religious Studies 11, no. 4 (1984): 293–311. Identifies Nakae Tōju (1608–1648) as "the founder of the Wang Yang-ming (Ōyōmei) school of philosophy in Japan" and explores his synthesis of Confucian, Taoist, Shinto, and Buddhist elements. Provides verified scholarly support for C025 (Nakae Tōju as founder of Japanese Yangmingism).
note: Dedicated journal article on Nakae Tōju as founder of Japanese Yangmingism (Ōyōmei-gaku). Published 8 years after the 1976 monograph. Provides specific, verifiable coverage of the Nakae Tōju claim. Added during passage-level verification sprint (2026-05-13).

title: Nakae Tōju and the Birth of Wang Yang-Ming Learning in Japan
author: Barry D. Steben
citation_detail: Steben, Barry D. "Nakae Tōju and the Birth of Wang Yang-Ming Learning in Japan." Monumenta Serica 46, no. 1 (1998): 233–263. DOI: 10.1080/02549948.1998.11731318. Covers the founding of Japanese Yangmingism (Ōyōmei-gaku) by Nakae Tōju (1608–1648). Provides specialist academic coverage of the transition of Wang Yangming's thought into Japan.
note: Specialist journal article on Nakae Tōju as founder of Japanese Yangmingism. Published in Monumenta Serica (peer-reviewed sinology journal). 9 citations. Provides academic coverage beyond Ching's monograph. Added during passage-level verification sprint (2026-05-13). Page range verified via Crossref (233-263). Specific page references for individual claims within this range still need verification against full text.

title: Japan: The Intellectual Foundations of Modern Japanese Politics
author: Tetsuo Najita
citation_detail: Najita, Tetsuo. Japan: The Intellectual Foundations of Modern Japanese Politics. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1980. ISBN 978-0-226-56803-4. 152 pp. VERIFIED (via Google Books 2026-05-13): Oyōmei (Wang Yangming) mentioned on p.54 re Ōshio Heihachirō. Takasugi Shinsaku on pp.61,64,65 (political actions, no Yangming link). Saigō Takamori: zero mentions in searchable content. No explicit link between Yangming thought and Bakumatsu figures. Chapter 3 (pp.43-68) covers Restorationism in Late Tokugawa.
note: General intellectual history of late Tokugawa-Meiji transition. ONLY verified Oyomei reference: p.54 (Oshio Heihachiro). Does NOT explicitly link Yangming thought to Saigo Takamori or Takasugi Shinsaku. Very weak support for C026. Consider adding a more specialized source on late Tokugawa Yangmingism.
